newsitem.title: UK: BAe at new high on positive results comment. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BAe at new high on positive results comment. [CORRECTED 11:50 GMT]

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc rose sharply for a second day on Friday, touching a record intraday high amid positive comment following the group's first-half results, traders said.
The stock was up 15p at 10.65-1/2 stg by 0803 GMT, after rising as high as 10.70 stg -- surpassing yesterday's peak of 10.65 stg.

Paul Pickford, analyst at Panmure Gordon, said he raised his 1996 pre-tax profit estimate to 407 million stg -- post exceptional interest -- giving 66.3p of earnings per share, and to 540 million stg or 85.3p for the year after.
Pickford said he has a medium-term target of 11.50 stg for the stock. "There is a lot of momentumn behind the stock and there is plenty of newsflow to maintain that momentum," he said.
Yesterday BAe posted a rise in headline first-half pre-tax profit to 199 million stg from 114 million a year before, and raised its dividend to 6.25p per share from 5p.
Pickford said his 11.50 target was only a conservative eight times expected 1997 earnings.

Zafar Khan at SG Strauss Turnbull said he raised his current year pre-tax estimate, also post-exceptional interest, to 415 million stg from 400 million and his forecast for next year to 515 million stg from 500 million (Corrects from "...forecast for next year to 440 million stg from 425 million.")
Khan also raised his six-month price target for the stock to 12.00 stg from 10.00 stg.

Khan said potential concerns could come into focus at some stage, such as the risk of political instability in Saudi Arabia, a major customer under the 10-year old Anglo-Saudi Al Yamamah oil for arms deal, and the cost of developing a new generation of Airbus aircraft.
"But for the time being there is momentum, BAe is producing the numbers and the dividend is going up strongly," Khan said. "There is no reason to rock the boat at the moment."
